# ADR-001: Autonomous Worktree Execution Platform

**Status:** Implementing
**Date:** 2025-07-01
**Authors:** Symphony Platform Team

---

## 1. Context

The current Symphony orchestration stack runs multiple AI agents in parallel across git worktrees (wt1–wt8). While the runner, integrator, state layer, and queue control are operational, the platform lacks **autonomous recovery** — dirty worktrees, failed commits, stuck leases, and integration conflicts require manual triage. This ADR defines the implementation program to close the gap between "parallel execution" and "fully autonomous operation."

## 2. Decision

Build a control-plane upgrade across six phases, each gated by acceptance criteria, to achieve unattended autonomous operation of the worktree fleet.

---

## 3. Gap Analysis

### What Already Exists

| Component         | File                                                                      | Status                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| State schema v2   | `harness/ops/core/symphony-state.mjs`                                     | ✅ Finalization states, integration queue/lock, sticky owner, lease/heartbeat, exponential backoff                                                                                                          |
| Integrator        | `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-integrator.mjs`                       | ✅ Single writer to main via cherry-pick, daemon mode, queue processing, conflict → `integration_failed_repairable`                                                                                         |
| Runner            | `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-runner.mjs`                           | ✅ Worktree detection, validation, commit, branch-only push, finalization state mgmt, sticky repair priority (`getNextRepairableIssueForWorktree` before `pickIssue`), continuation, failure fingerprinting |
| Worktree config   | `harness/ops/core/worktree-config.mjs`                                    | ✅ Paths, branch naming, Discord/Symphony routing                                                                                                                                                           |
| Worktree pool     | `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-worktree-pool.mjs`                    | ✅ Create, cleanup, repair, list                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Queue control     | `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-queue-control.mjs`                    | ✅ Feed, drain, enforce concurrency, detect stuck work                                                                                                                                                      |
| Config            | `harness/ops/core/symphony-config.mjs`                                    | ✅ Timing chain, retry limits, concurrency                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Systemd services  | `services/systemd/anqr-symphony-*`                                        | ✅ executor@, integrator, runner, watchdog, router                                                                                                                                                          |
| Unit tests        | `tests/unit/finalization-state.spec.ts`                                   | ✅ Finalization CRUD, queue dedup, lock exclusivity, repair candidate lookup                                                                                                                                |
| Integration tests | `tests/integration/symphony-integrator.spec.ts`                           | ✅ Queue flow, conflict handling, sticky owner preservation                                                                                                                                                 |
| Recovery tools    | `harness/ops/tools/recover-stale-in-progress.mjs`, `startup-recovery.mjs` | ✅ Partial — stale lease cleanup, service restart                                                                                                                                                           |
| Watchdog          | `harness/ops/runtime/symphony/watchdog-monitor.mjs`                       | ✅ Bridge health, log analysis, auto-rollback                                                                                                                                                               |

### What Is Missing

| Gap ID  | Requirement                                                                                        | Current State                                                            | Severity                                               |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| **G1**  | Recovery daemon (scan → classify → repair → quarantine)                                            | Does not exist                                                           | **Critical** — no autonomous dirty worktree resolution |
| **G2**  | `validation_failed_repairable` finalization state                                                  | Validation failures `gitRevert()` + return to Todo                       | **High** — loses work, violates repair-first principle |
| **G3**  | `RUNNER_AUTO_PUSH = false`                                                                         | Branch→integrator flow disabled                                          | **Blocker** — integrator never receives candidates     |
| **G4**  | Explicit worktree state tracking (`available`/`executing`/`dirty`/`quarantined`)                   | Implicit — no per-worktree state in shared store                         | **High** — scheduler cannot make informed decisions    |
| **G5**  | Quarantine model with reprovisioning                                                               | Uses `Backlog` + `retry_exhausted` as proxy                              | **Medium** — no formal quarantine/reprovision workflow |
| **G6**  | Machine-readable fleet health inventory                                                            | No dedicated health snapshot                                             | **Medium** — not externally observable                 |
| **G7**  | End-to-end simulation harness                                                                      | Does not exist                                                           | **Medium** — cannot prove autonomy                     |
| **G8**  | Deprecated `gitPush()` still exists                                                                | Dead code in runner                                                      | **Low** — cleanup                                      |
| **G9**  | Integrator re-enqueue after repair                                                                 | No automatic re-enqueue when `integration_failed_repairable` is repaired | **Medium** — requires manual intervention              |
| **G10** | `RUNNER_MAX_RETRIES = Infinity`                                                                    | No bounded retries — violates spec requirement                           | **High** — repair loops can cycle forever              |
| **G11** | Bridge commit/push audit                                                                           | Bridge may have auto-commit/push paths in runner flows                   | **Medium** — spec requires bridge never auto-commits   |
| **G12** | Explicit issue execution states (`locally_validated`, `local_commit_complete`, `branch_published`) | Currently implicit in runner flow, not tracked in state model            | **Medium** — reduces observability                     |

---

## 4. Target Architecture

### 4.1 Four Autonomous Loops

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Shared Durable State                      │
│              harness/ops/core/symphony-state.mjs             │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ issues{} │  │ worktrees{}  │  │ global.integrationQueue│ │
│  │ leases   │  │ state per wt │  │ global.integrationLock │ │
│  │ finalize │  │ quarantine   │  │ global.fleetSnapshot   │ │
│  └──────────┘  └──────────────┘  └────────────────────────┘ │
└──────────┬──────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┬─────────┘
           │          │              │              │
     ┌─────▼────┐ ┌───▼────────┐ ┌──▼──────────┐ ┌▼──────────────┐
     │Scheduler │ │  Executor  │ │  Recovery   │ │  Integrator   │
     │  Loop    │ │   Loop     │ │  Daemon     │ │  (single      │
     │(queue-   │ │(runner per │ │  Loop       │ │   writer)     │
     │ control) │ │ worktree)  │ │             │ │               │
     └──────────┘ └────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └───────────────┘
```

### 4.2 Worktree State Machine

```
                    ┌──────────┐
        ┌──────────►│available │◄────────────────────────────┐
        │           └────┬─────┘                             │
        │                │ scheduler assigns                 │
        │           ┌────▼─────┐                             │
        │           │executing │                             │
        │           └────┬─────┘                             │
        │                │                                   │
        │     ┌──────────┼──────────────┐                    │
        │     │          │              │                    │
        │  ┌──▼───┐  ┌──▼──────┐  ┌────▼────────────┐       │
        │  │commit│  │validate │  │ branch_push      │       │
        │  │failed│  │failed   │  │ failed           │       │
        │  │repair│  │repair   │  │ repairable       │       │
        │  └──┬───┘  └──┬──────┘  └────┬─────────────┘       │
        │     │          │              │                    │
        │     └──────────┼──────────────┘                    │
        │                │ repair succeeds                   │
        │           ┌────▼─────────────┐                     │
        │           │integration       │                     │
        │           │pending           │                     │
        │           └────┬─────────────┘                     │
        │                │                                   │
        │     ┌──────────┼──────────┐                        │
        │     │                     │                        │
        │  ┌──▼───────────┐   ┌────▼────────────┐           │
        │  │integrated    │   │integration      │           │
        │  │main (Done)   │   │failed_repairable│──repair──►│
        │  └──────────────┘   └─────────────────┘           │
        │                                                    │
        │  quarantine after max retries                      │
        │  ┌──────────────┐   ┌──────────────┐              │
        └──│reprovisioned │◄──│ quarantined  │              │
           └──────────────┘   └──────────────┘
```

---

## 5. Implementation Plan

### Phase 0: Observability & State Hardening

**Goal:** Make the fleet observable enough to safely automate recovery.

#### New Files

| File                                   | Responsibility                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `harness/ops/core/worktree-health.mjs` | Per-worktree health snapshot + fleet inventory |
| `tests/unit/worktree-health.spec.ts`   | Health snapshot classification tests           |

#### Modifications

| File                                    | Change                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `harness/ops/core/symphony-state.mjs`   | Add `store.worktreeStates` map, `setWorktreeState()`, `getWorktreeState()`, `listWorktreesByState()`, `getFleetSnapshot()` |
| `tests/unit/finalization-state.spec.ts` | Add worktree state CRUD tests                                                                                              |

#### Interface: `worktree-health.mjs`

```javascript
/**
 * @param {string} worktreeId - e.g. "wt1"
 * @returns {{
 *   id: string,
 *   path: string,
 *   exists: boolean,
 *   gitDirtyFiles: string[],
 *   branch: string,
 *   headSha: string,
 *   finalizationState: object|null,
 *   leaseState: object|null,
 *   classification: 'available'|'executing'|'dirty_owned'|'dirty_orphaned'|'quarantined'|'blocked',
 *   issueIdentifier: string|null,
 *   updatedAt: string
 * }}
 */
export function getWorktreeHealthSnapshot(worktreeId) {}

/**
 * @returns {{
 *   worktrees: Snapshot[],
 *   summary: { available: number, executing: number, dirty: number, quarantined: number, blocked: number },
 *   timestamp: string
 * }}
 */
export function getFleetInventory() {}
```

#### Interface: State model additions in `symphony-state.mjs`

```javascript
// New store shape additions:
// store.worktreeStates = {
//   "wt1": { state: "available", issueIdentifier: null, updatedAt: "..." },
//   "wt2": { state: "executing", issueIdentifier: "ANQ-123", updatedAt: "..." },
//   "wt3": { state: "quarantined", issueIdentifier: "ANQ-456", reason: "...", quarantinedAt: "...", repairAttempts: 3, lastError: "..." }
// }

export function setWorktreeState(worktreeId, patch) {}
export function getWorktreeState(worktreeId) {}
export function listWorktreesByState(state) {}
export function recordQuarantine(worktreeId, details) {}
export function clearQuarantine(worktreeId) {}
```

#### State Migration

Adding `store.worktreeStates` requires no explicit migration. The existing `loadState()` normalizer already falls back to defaults for missing fields via `emptyStore()`. Phase 0 must:

- Extend `emptyStore()` to include `worktreeStates: {}`
- Add normalization in `loadState()` for the new field
- Add a schema migration test that loads a v2 state file without `worktreeStates` and verifies it round-trips correctly

#### Gate 0 Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `getWorktreeHealthSnapshot()` returns correct classification for clean, dirty, leased, and quarantined worktrees
- [ ] `getFleetInventory()` produces valid JSON with summary counts
- [ ] `setWorktreeState()` / `getWorktreeState()` round-trip correctly
- [ ] Stale lock expiry tests pass
- [ ] State migration: loading existing v2 state.json without `worktreeStates` produces valid store
- [ ] All Phase 0 unit tests pass: `npx vitest run tests/unit/worktree-health.spec.ts tests/unit/finalization-state.spec.ts`

---

### Phase 1: Remove Unsafe Finalization Paths

**Goal:** Enable the branch→integrator flow and eliminate dead code paths.

#### Modifications

| File                                            | Change                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `harness/ops/core/symphony-config.mjs`          | Set `RUNNER_AUTO_PUSH = true`. Set `RUNNER_MAX_RETRIES = 10` (bounded — spec requires finite retries; Infinity violates repair-first model).           |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-runner.mjs` | Remove deprecated `gitPush()` function (~80 lines). Add `setWorktreeState('executing')` on issue start, `setWorktreeState('available')` on clean exit. |

#### Gate 1 Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `RUNNER_AUTO_PUSH = true` — runner successfully pushes to worktree branch
- [ ] `RUNNER_MAX_RETRIES` is finite (≤ 10)
- [ ] Integrator receives candidates via integration queue
- [ ] `git grep 'push.*origin.*HEAD:main' harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-runner.mjs` returns zero matches
- [ ] Deprecated `gitPush()` function removed from runner
- [ ] Bridge audit: `git grep 'git.*push\|git.*commit' harness/ops/bridges/` confirms bridge does not auto-commit or push in runner flows
- [ ] Integration test: runner commit → branch push → integration queue entry created
- [ ] `npx vitest run tests/integration/symphony-integrator.spec.ts` passes

---

### Phase 2: Complete Sticky Repair Model

**Goal:** Preserve dirty trees for repair instead of reverting validated work.

#### Modifications

| File                                            | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `harness/ops/core/symphony-state.mjs`           | Add `"validation_failed_repairable"` to `REPAIRABLE_FINALIZATION_STATES`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `harness/ops/core/symphony-config.mjs`          | Add `RUNNER_VALIDATION_REPAIR_MAX = 3` — max same-worktree validation repair cycles before quarantine                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-runner.mjs` | **Behavioral change:** When validation fails and `finalization.attempts < RUNNER_VALIDATION_REPAIR_MAX`, set `validation_failed_repairable` finalization state with sticky owner instead of `gitRevert()` + return to Todo. Preserve dirty tree. Store full validation output (not truncated) in `lastError` or a sidecar file at `.git/SYMPHONY_VALIDATION_ERRORS`. On next cycle, sticky repair picks it up and continues with validation error context. |
| `tests/unit/finalization-state.spec.ts`         | Add: `validation_failed_repairable` is returned by `getNextRepairableIssueForWorktree()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

#### New Runner Validation Failure Flow

```
Before (current):
  validation fails → gitRevert() → return to Todo → fresh start

After (target):
  validation fails (attempt < RUNNER_VALIDATION_REPAIR_MAX) →
    setFinalizationState("validation_failed_repairable", {
      stickyOwner: WORKTREE_ID,
      lastError: validation stderr (truncated summary),
      attempts: N
    }) →
    write full validation output to .git/SYMPHONY_VALIDATION_ERRORS →
    updateIssue(STATES.inReview) →
    dirty tree preserved →
    next cycle: getNextRepairableIssueForWorktree() picks it up →
    runner sends validation errors as repair prompt →
    agent fixes in same worktree with preserved context

  validation fails (attempt >= threshold) →
    gitRevert() → quarantine to Backlog (existing behavior)
```

#### Gate 2 Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Validation failure sets `validation_failed_repairable` in finalization state
- [ ] Same worktree picks up repair issue on next runner cycle
- [ ] Repair prompt includes validation error details
- [ ] After successful repair + validation pass → commit + push to branch
- [ ] Repeated same-signature validation failure → quarantine (existing fingerprinting)
- [ ] `npx vitest run tests/unit/finalization-state.spec.ts` passes with new state

---

### Phase 3: Recovery Daemon

**Goal:** Autonomously drain dirty worktrees back to healthy state.

#### New Files

| File                                                       | Responsibility                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-worktree-recovery.mjs` | Scan → classify → repair → quarantine loop |
| `services/systemd/anqr-symphony-worktree-recovery.service` | Systemd unit                               |
| `tests/unit/worktree-recovery.spec.ts`                     | Classification + state machine unit tests  |
| `tests/integration/recovery-daemon.spec.ts`                | Repair dispatch integration tests          |

#### Interface: `symphony-worktree-recovery.mjs`

```javascript
/**
 * Classify a worktree's current state and determine repair action.
 * @param {HealthSnapshot} snapshot - from worktree-health.mjs
 * @returns {{
 *   classification: 'clean'|'dirty_owned'|'dirty_orphaned'|'stale_lease'|'conflicted'|'half_committed',
 *   confidence: number,  // 0.0–1.0 (threshold: RECOVERY_OWNERSHIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD),
 *   inferredOwner: string|null,
 *   repairAction: 'continue_repair'|'retry_push'|'retry_commit'|'quarantine'|'reprovision'|'skip'|null
 * }}
 */
export function classifyWorktree(snapshot) {}

/**
 * Execute repair action on a worktree.
 * @returns {{ ok: boolean, action: string, nextState: string, error?: string }}
 */
export async function executeRepair(worktreeId, classification) {}

/**
 * Run one full recovery cycle across all worktrees.
 * @returns {{ scanned: number, repaired: number, quarantined: number, skipped: number, errors: string[] }}
 */
export async function runRecoveryCycle() {}

/** Daemon mode: poll loop with configurable interval. */
export async function runDaemon() {}

/** CLI: once | daemon | status */
```

#### Classification Logic

```
Input: worktree health snapshot

1. No dirty files + no active finalization → 'clean' → skip
2. Active lease with recent heartbeat → 'executing' → skip (runner is alive)
3. Dirty files + finalization.stickyOwner matches worktree:
   → 'dirty_owned' / high confidence
   → repairAction: 'continue_repair'
4. Dirty files + stale/expired lease:
   → 'stale_lease'
   → release lease, attempt ownership inference from branch + recent commits
   → if confident: 'dirty_owned' → 'continue_repair'
   → if not: 'dirty_orphaned' → 'quarantine'
5. Dirty files + no finalization + no lease:
   → 'dirty_orphaned' / confidence < RECOVERY_OWNERSHIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD
   → attempt inference from branch name, git log, recent state transitions
   → if confident: reassign ownership → 'continue_repair'
   → if not: 'quarantine'
6. Commit exists but push failed:
   → 'half_committed'
   → 'retry_push'
7. Merge conflict markers in files:
   → 'conflicted'
   → 'quarantine' (conflict resolution requires AI context)
```

#### Recovery Config (added to `symphony-config.mjs`)

```javascript
export const RECOVERY_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000; // 1 min scan interval
export const RECOVERY_MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS = 5; // per worktree before quarantine
export const RECOVERY_QUARANTINE_THRESHOLD_MS = 600_000; // 10 min stuck in repairable → quarantine
export const RECOVERY_STALE_LEASE_GRACE_MS = 300_000; // 5 min grace before reclaiming lease
export const RECOVERY_OWNERSHIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.7;
```

#### Gate 3 Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Daemon detects dirty worktree with known owner → dispatches repair
- [ ] Daemon detects dirty orphan with low confidence → quarantines
- [ ] Bounded retries → `blocked` / `quarantined` transition after `RECOVERY_MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS`
- [ ] Clean repaired worktree returns to `available` state
- [ ] Orphaned worktree quarantine does not auto-commit
- [ ] `npx vitest run tests/unit/worktree-recovery.spec.ts tests/integration/recovery-daemon.spec.ts` passes
- [ ] `systemctl --user start anqr-symphony-worktree-recovery` runs without error

---

### Phase 4: Harden Integrator

**Goal:** Make integration conflict-safe and support repair re-enqueue.

#### Modifications

| File                                                | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-integrator.mjs` | (1) After `integration_failed_repairable` is repaired and branch re-pushed, automatically re-enqueue via a recovery-daemon hook or periodic queue scan. (2) `git fetch` the specific branch ref before cherry-pick to handle force-pushed branches after conflict repair. (3) Add metric logging for integration latency. |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-runner.mjs`     | After successful repair of `integration_failed_repairable` → re-push branch → `enqueueIntegrationCandidate()` → set state back to `integration_pending`                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `tests/integration/symphony-integrator.spec.ts`     | Add: re-enqueue-after-repair test, force-pushed branch handling test, two-branch serial integration test                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

#### Gate 4 Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Two published worktree branches integrate one at a time (lock enforced)
- [ ] Conflict does not mark Done — marks `integration_failed_repairable`
- [ ] Repaired branch is re-enqueued automatically after re-push
- [ ] Force-pushed branch (new headSha) is fetched correctly
- [ ] `npx vitest run tests/integration/symphony-integrator.spec.ts` passes

---

### Phase 5: Fleet Health & Reprovisioning

**Goal:** Self-heal over long unattended runs.

#### New Files

| File                                            | Responsibility                         |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `services/systemd/anqr-worktree-health.timer`   | Periodic health snapshot (every 5 min) |
| `services/systemd/anqr-worktree-health.service` | One-shot health check                  |

#### Modifications

| File                                                       | Change                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-worktree-pool.mjs`     | Add `reprovisionWorktree(id)` — force-remove + recreate from `origin/main`, reinstall deps, reset upstream                                                                                 |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-worktree-recovery.mjs` | Add reprovisioning path: quarantined worktree with `repairAttempts >= RECOVERY_MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS` → call `reprovisionWorktree()` → `clearQuarantine()` → `setWorktreeState('available')` |
| `harness/ops/core/worktree-health.mjs`                     | Add `writeFleetHealthFile()` — persist JSON to `reports/symphony/fleet-health.json` for external observability                                                                             |

#### Gate 5 Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Crashed runner's lease expires → recovery picks up within `RECOVERY_STALE_LEASE_GRACE_MS`
- [ ] Quarantined worktree is reprovisioned automatically after threshold
- [ ] Reprovisioned worktree passes health check and returns to `available`
- [ ] Poisoned worktree does not receive new work (scheduler checks worktree state)
- [ ] `reports/symphony/fleet-health.json` is machine-readable and updated periodically
- [ ] `systemctl --user status anqr-worktree-health.timer` shows active

---

### Phase 6: Closed-Loop Autonomy Verification

**Goal:** Prove unattended operation across mixed failure modes.

#### New Files

| File                                    | Responsibility                                     |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `tests/e2e/autonomy-simulation.spec.ts` | End-to-end simulation harness with fault injection |

#### Scenarios

| #   | Scenario                                              | Expected Outcome                                                          |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | AI edits introduce lint errors                        | Recovery loop fixes and publishes → integrator promotes to main           |
| 2   | Two worktrees touch same file, both publish           | First integrates, second conflicts → repair → second integrates           |
| 3   | Executor crashes mid-edit                             | Stale lease expires → recovery resumes → issue completes                  |
| 4   | Dirty orphaned worktree with low-confidence ownership | Quarantine → scheduler uses remaining healthy pool                        |
| 5   | Kill runner during validation                         | Recovery classifies `validation_failed_repairable` → same-worktree repair |
| 6   | Break network during push                             | `branch_push_failed_repairable` → retry → succeeds → integrates           |
| 7   | Corrupt lock holder process                           | Stale lock detected → released → execution resumes                        |
| 8   | Integration crashes while lock held                   | TTL expires → next cycle acquires lock → continues                        |

#### SLO Targets

| Metric                                     | Target       |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------ |
| Dirty worktree detection                   | < 2 minutes  |
| Repair reassignment to same worktree       | < 2 minutes  |
| Quarantine decision for irrecoverable tree | < 10 minutes |
| Integration queue latency (normal load)    | < 5 minutes  |
| Stale lease recovery                       | < 10 minutes |
| Main promotion concurrency violations      | 0            |

#### Gate 6 Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 8 simulation scenarios pass
- [ ] Overnight unattended run completes mixed workloads
- [ ] All SLO targets met across 24-hour window
- [ ] No dirty worktree blocks the whole platform
- [ ] Zero human interventions required for routine failures

---

## 6. File Inventory Summary

### New Files (9)

| File                                                       | Phase |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `harness/ops/core/worktree-health.mjs`                     | 0     |
| `tests/unit/worktree-health.spec.ts`                       | 0     |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-worktree-recovery.mjs` | 3     |
| `tests/unit/worktree-recovery.spec.ts`                     | 3     |
| `tests/integration/recovery-daemon.spec.ts`                | 3     |
| `services/systemd/anqr-symphony-worktree-recovery.service` | 3     |
| `services/systemd/anqr-worktree-health.service`            | 5     |
| `services/systemd/anqr-worktree-health.timer`              | 5     |
| `tests/e2e/autonomy-simulation.spec.ts`                    | 6     |

### Modified Files (8)

| File                                                   | Phases    |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------- |
| `harness/ops/core/symphony-state.mjs`                  | 0, 2      |
| `harness/ops/core/symphony-config.mjs`                 | 1, 2, 3   |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-runner.mjs`        | 1, 2, 4   |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-integrator.mjs`    | 4         |
| `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-worktree-pool.mjs` | 5         |
| `tests/unit/finalization-state.spec.ts`                | 0, 2      |
| `tests/integration/symphony-integrator.spec.ts`        | 4         |
| `docs/adrs/#10`       | This file |

---

## 7. Critical Path

```
Phase 0 ──► Phase 1 ──► Phase 2 ──► Phase 3 ──► Phase 4 ──► Phase 5 ──► Phase 6
  │            │            │            │            │            │
  │ health     │ enable     │ validation │ recovery   │ harden     │ reprovision
  │ snapshot   │ auto-push  │ repairable │ daemon     │ integrator │ + health
  │            │ rm dead    │ state      │            │            │ service
  │            │ code       │            │            │            │
  ▼            ▼            ▼            ▼            ▼            ▼
Gate 0      Gate 1       Gate 2       Gate 3       Gate 4       Gate 5 → Gate 6
```

**Phases 0–3 are strictly sequential** — each depends on the prior phase's output.
**Phase 4 can overlap with Phase 3** — integrator hardening is independent of recovery daemon.
**Phase 5 depends on Phases 3 and 4** — reprovisioning needs recovery daemon + integrator.
**Phase 6 depends on all prior phases.**

---

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk                                                                    | Impact | Mitigation                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enabling `RUNNER_AUTO_PUSH` causes cascading integrator failures        | High   | Gate 1 requires integration test passing before proceeding. Roll back config if failures detected. |
| `validation_failed_repairable` preserves bad state that blocks worktree | Medium | Bounded attempts (existing `RUNNER_MAX_VALIDATION_FIXES`). After threshold → revert + quarantine.  |
| Recovery daemon misclassifies executing worktree as dirty               | High   | Skip worktrees with active lease AND recent heartbeat. Grace period before any action.             |
| Reprovisioning destroys forensic evidence                               | Low    | Quarantine period before reprovision. Health file preserves snapshot at quarantine time.           |
| Overnight chaos soak reveals unknown failure modes                      | Medium | Phase 6 is verification — failures discovered here feed back into prior phases.                    |

---

## 9. Validation Commands

Each phase's gate should be verified with:

```bash
# Unit tests (single-threaded, flock-serialized)
flock -w 120 9 npx vitest run tests/unit/worktree-health.spec.ts 9>/tmp/anqr-vitest.lock
flock -w 120 9 npx vitest run tests/unit/finalization-state.spec.ts 9>/tmp/anqr-vitest.lock
flock -w 120 9 npx vitest run tests/unit/worktree-recovery.spec.ts 9>/tmp/anqr-vitest.lock

# Integration tests
flock -w 120 9 npx vitest run tests/integration/symphony-integrator.spec.ts 9>/tmp/anqr-vitest.lock
flock -w 120 9 npx vitest run tests/integration/recovery-daemon.spec.ts 9>/tmp/anqr-vitest.lock

# Safety grep: no direct main push outside integrator
git grep 'push.*origin.*HEAD:main' harness/ops/orchestration/ | grep -v symphony-integrator

# Typecheck
flock -w 120 9 npx tsc --noEmit 9>/tmp/anqr-typecheck.lock
```

---

## 10. Definition of Done

The platform is **fully autonomous** when:

1. Work begins without human dispatch
2. Failures are detected automatically (< 2 min)
3. Same-worktree repair is automatic
4. Branch publication is automatic
5. Main integration is automatic and serialized
6. Stuck/dirty/orphaned worktrees are autonomously drained, quarantined, or reprovisioned
7. Normal scheduling resumes after recovery without human intervention
8. Human intervention is needed only for true policy exceptions or repeated irrecoverable failures
9. All of the above is externally observable via machine-readable health status

---

## 11. Next Step

Create Linear issues for each phase, starting with Phase 0 (worktree-health.mjs + state model additions). Each phase should be a single issue with its gate criteria as the acceptance checklist.

# ADR-0002: Symphony Reboot on Main

## Decision

Rebuild Symphony from scratch on `main` as a smaller, stricter autonomous operations substrate. Do not copy legacy `master` files.

## Reason

Legacy `master` accumulated operational complexity that obscured the working core. The real work is not migration — it is distilling legacy lessons into a tighter system.

## Key Lessons from Legacy

### Deterministic first

Symphony worked when the loop began with deterministic local checks, not AI reasoning. The three-tier corrective framework is:

1. local deterministic checks (harness-report)
2. scheduled automation (nightly-ops-pass)
3. issue-driven AI correction (Symphony execution)

### Ollama is single-slot

- `max_concurrent_agents` = 1
- `num_thread` = 1
- Issues must be Ollama-sized: 1–2 files, 1–3 acceptance criteria, single run <5 minutes
- Throughput targets: 2–3 queued items, not 5–10
- GPU contention, timeouts, and `provider_no_output` failures are the dominant failure mode

### Guardian over Sentinel

The AI-first Sentinel pattern was replaced with deterministic Guardian checks. Guardian owns:

- reading harness reports
- creating/updating issues
- duplicate suppression
- queue-size control
- stale-session escalation
- hygiene enforcement

### Hygiene must be automatic

- Required priority + domain/risk labels on all issues
- Descriptor taxonomy: `[CHILD]`, `[HUMAN]`, `[LOCAL-SLICE]`
- Queue health actively drained
- Human-only items clearly marked and excluded from automation

### systemd environment differs

PATH and runtime environment under systemd differ from interactive shells. Service units must set explicit PATH, HOME, and NODE_PATH.

## Structure

```
harness/ops/       operational scripts (harness, guardian, audit, routing)
services/systemd/   systemd service and timer units
reports/            harness report artifacts
docs/workflows/     execution workflow documentation
```

## Phased Delivery

See ANQ-364 and children (ANQ-365 through ANQ-371).

# ADR-0003: All-in-One Symphony Bridge with Integrated Codebuff SDK

**Status:** Accepted  
**Date:** 2026-03-31  
**Deciders:** Harness Team  
**Reviewers:** GPT-5 (external architecture review)

## Context

The ANQR harness uses AI bridges to enable LLM-driven task execution across multiple git worktrees for concurrent processing. The original architecture had separate services:

1. **Codebuff Bridge** (`anqr-codebuff-bridge@.service`) — Codebuff SDK exposed as OpenAI HTTP API
2. **Symphony Bridge** (`anqr-symphony-executor@.service`, was `anqr-symphony-bridge@.service`) — AI completion with provider cascade and tool execution
3. **Discord Router** (`anqr-discord-router.service`) — Load balancer that rewrites cwd to target worktrees

### The Fundamental Problem

During external code review, a critical defect was identified in `codebuff-openai-bridge.mjs`:

**F1: Codebuff client cwd caching** — The shared Codebuff client was keyed by `costMode` only, ignoring the working directory (`cwd`). This meant:

- Requests intended for worktree `wt1` could silently reuse a client created with `cwd=/home/user/src/anqr-wt2`
- File operations would execute in the wrong worktree
- Worktree isolation was broken at the bridge level

While this was fixed by keying the client by `costMode + cwd`, it revealed a deeper architectural issue: **shared services across worktrees introduce caching and state management complexity that breaks isolation guarantees.**

## Decision

**Consolidate Codebuff bridge functionality, routing logic, and Symphony bridge into a single "all-in-one Symphony bridge" per worktree.**

Each Symphony executor instance (`anqr-symphony-executor@{1-8}.service`) will:

1. Handle AI completion requests (`/v1/chat/completions`)
2. Execute Codebuff SDK operations (tool use, code edits, file operations)
3. Run within its designated worktree via systemd `WorkingDirectory`
4. Maintain its own isolated provider cascade and session state
5. Automatically sync from `origin/main` before each request and push changes after completion

This eliminates:

- The separate Codebuff bridge service (`anqr-codebuff-bridge@.service`)
- The need for explicit cwd rewriting in the router (WorkingDirectory ensures correct cwd)
- Caching complexity across worktrees (each bridge is self-contained)

## Architecture

### Before (3-layer architecture)

```
Discord Gateway (OpenClaw) → Discord Router (port 18790)
                               ↓ rewrites cwd, selects worktree
                             Worktree Symphony Bridges (ports 4325-4328)
                               ↓ AI completion only
                             Provider Cascade → LLM API

Separate: Codebuff Bridge (port 4318, 4331-4338)
                               ↓ Codebuff SDK operations
                             Shared client cache (defect F1)
```

### After (2-layer architecture)

```
Discord Gateway (OpenClaw) → Discord Router (port 18790)
                               ↓ selects worktree, proxies request
                             All-in-One Symphony Bridges (ports 4325-4328)
                               ↓ AI completion + Codebuff SDK + tool execution
                               ↓ WorkingDirectory = worktree path
                             Provider Cascade → LLM API
```

Each Symphony bridge is:

- **Self-contained:** All capabilities (AI, tools, Codebuff SDK) in one service
- **Worktree-bound:** systemd `WorkingDirectory` ensures correct cwd from process start
- **Isolated:** No shared state or caching across worktrees

## Consequences

### Positive

- **Eliminates caching defects:** No shared client state across worktrees
- **Simplifies isolation model:** WorkingDirectory is the single source of truth for worktree binding
- **Reduces service count:** Eliminates 8 separate Codebuff bridge instances (wt1-wt8)
- **Clearer architecture:** One service per worktree instead of multiple overlapping services
- **Easier to reason about:** No cwd rewriting logic needed (WorkingDirectory handles it)

### Negative

- **Code duplication in each bridge:** Codebuff SDK integration code now in every Symphony bridge instance (but they're the same systemd template)
- **Memory overhead:** Each bridge loads full capability set even if only AI completion is needed (acceptable tradeoff)

### Migration Path

1. **Phase 1:** Integrate Codebuff SDK directly into `symphony-openai-bridge.mjs`
2. **Phase 2:** Update Symphony bridge instances to expose Codebuff capabilities
3. **Phase 3:** Deprecate and disable Codebuff bridge services
4. **Phase 4:** Update documentation and remove deprecated service files

## Implementation Notes

- Symphony bridge already has tool execution framework — extend it to support Codebuff SDK methods
- Router simplification: can reduce cwd rewriting logic (WorkingDirectory is authoritative)
- Service deployment: update only `anqr-symphony-executor@.service` template
- Backward compatibility: Main bridge (port 4319) remains unchanged for non-worktree use cases

## Related ADRs

- ADR-0001: Bootstrap branch strategy (establishes worktree foundation)
- ADR-0002: Symphony reboot (establishes AI bridge architecture)

## References

- External code review findings (2026-03-31): F1, F2, F3
- `docs/harness/12-concurrent-execution-with-worktrees.md` (Phase 0-8 validation)
- `docs/harness/discord-worktree-routing.md` (Discord isolation architecture)
- `services/systemd/anqr-codebuff-bridge@.service` (deprecated)

14. [workspace/README.md](/home/user/src/anqr/docs/harness/workspace/README.md)

## Scope

This section governs:

- `harness/ops/*`
- `services/systemd/*`
- the fresh Linear workspace model
- evidence and gate policy for agent-driven delivery

It does not redefine the product architecture itself. For that, use [README.md](/home/user/src/anqr/README.md) and [docs/program/01-anqr-1.0-definition.md](/home/user/src/anqr/docs/program/01-anqr-1.0-definition.md).

# Harness Operating Model

The harness exists to run governed engineering work with minimal human supervision while staying truthful about scope, quality, and escalation.

## Core loop

The maintained control flow is:

`harness-report -> linear-guardian -> queue control -> symphony runner -> notify`

Supporting jobs:

- nightly ops pass
- email ingest
- Sonar sync and audit
- provider credit/routing checks

## Surfaces

- `harness/ops/*`
  - canonical harness runtime
- `services/systemd/*`
  - canonical local operator automation runtime
- Linear
  - issue system of record for active work
- reports
  - generated evidence and operational output

## Required behavior

- keep the harness separate from product request-path code
- keep launch truth in docs, not in prompt fragments
- prefer dry-run and evidence-first modes before mutation
- escalate secrets, approvals, billing, and launch-claim changes to humans

## Degraded mode

The harness must remain usable in reduced environments:

- with provider fallbacks
- with queue dry-runs instead of mutation
- with public MCP/API running even if authenticated hardening is not enabled

When degraded, the system must say so explicitly instead of pretending full capability.

# Runtime And Services

This document defines the maintained harness/runtime surfaces.

## Canonical runtime roots

- `harness/ops/*`
- `services/systemd/*`

## Maintained scripts

Control loop:

- `harness/ops/harness-report.mjs`
- `harness/ops/linear-guardian.mjs`
- `harness/ops/symphony-queue-control.mjs`
- `harness/ops/symphony-runner.mjs` — compatibility shim to `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-runner.mjs`
- `harness/ops/symphony-agent.mjs`
- `harness/ops/nightly-ops-pass.mjs`

Integrations and support:

- `harness/ops/email-ingest.mjs`
- `harness/ops/lib/notify.mjs`
- `harness/ops/sonar-linear-mail.mjs`
- `harness/ops/symphony-credit-gate.mjs`
- `harness/ops/integrations/model/symphony-openai-bridge.mjs` — AI SDK-based bridge with tool execution
- `harness/ops/integrations/model/codebuff-direct.mjs` — Codebuff SDK execution (runs inside each worktree-local bridge)
- `harness/ops/integrations/model/symphony-agent-router.mjs` — Control-plane router for worktree-local bridges
- `harness/ops/integrations/model/symphony-adaptive-context.mjs` — dynamic per-provider token ceilings and rate management
- `harness/ops/integrations/model/symphony-bridge-truncation.mjs` — static token limits and message truncation
- `harness/ops/integrations/model/ollama-local-audit.mjs`
- `harness/ops/integrations/model/codebuff-sdk-runner.mjs` (DEPRECATED, exports shared constants only)
- `harness/ops/linear-all.mjs` — Fetches all backlog issues from Linear
- `harness/ops/linear-issue-review.mjs` — One-time issue review and correction
- `harness/ops/integrations/linear/linear-client.mjs` — Linear API helper library
- `harness/ops/harness-doctor.mjs` — Runtime diagnostics and health checks
- `harness/ops/integrations/sonar/sonar-linear-audit.mjs` — Nightly SonarQube to Linear sync
- `harness/ops/notifications/notify-impl.mjs` — Notification implementation details (path constants)

RAG pipeline and search:

- `harness/ops/lib/rag/chunker.mjs` — Semantic code/document chunker (function/class/heading boundaries)
- `harness/ops/lib/rag/embeddings.mjs` — Ollama embedding generation (`qwen2.5-coder:3b-instruct`)
- `harness/ops/lib/rag/vector-store.mjs` — File-based vector store in `reports/rag-index/` with incremental indexing
- `harness/ops/lib/rag/build-index.mjs` — Full-repo RAG index builder using `git ls-files` (respects .gitignore)
- `harness/ops/lib/search/hybrid-search.mjs` — BM25 + semantic search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)

MCP runtime:

- `harness/ops/runtime/mcp/context7-server.mjs` — Local Context7 MCP server wrapper (JSON-RPC over stdio)
- `harness/ops/runtime/mcp/context7-http-service.mjs` — HTTP service wrapping Context7 MCP (port 4320)

Restructured copies under subdirectories may exist. The root entrypoints remain the stable operator contract until a deliberate cleanup replaces them.

## Systemd units

Scheduled automation:

- `anqr-linear-runner@.service` / `.timer` — Linear issue poller and scheduler (wt1-wt4)
- `anqr-queue-feeder.service` / `.timer`
- `anqr-nightly.service` / `.timer` — 02:00 daily
- `anqr-rag-rebuild.service` / `.timer` — 03:00 daily, full-repo RAG vector index rebuild via Ollama embeddings
- `anqr-email-ingest.service` / `.timer`

Long-running services:

- `anqr-symphony-router.service` — Global Symphony orchestration (control plane, port 4319)
- `anqr-symphony-executor@.service` — Worktree-local Symphony executors (ports 4321-4328)
- `anqr-discord-router.service` — Discord request load balancer (port 18790)
- `anqr-context7-mcp.service` — Context7 MCP documentation service (HTTP on port 4320)
- `anqr-watchdog.service` — Health monitoring

Note: Codebuff is a provider used by executors, not a standalone service (per ADR-0003).

**CRITICAL: Before restarting any bridge service:**

1. **STOP task execution**: `node harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-control.mjs --stop`
2. **Wait for zero concurrency**: Check `symphony-runner.mjs --status` and Discord for "(0 concurrent)"
3. **Restart service**: `systemctl --user restart <service-name>`
4. **RESTART task execution**: `node harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-control.mjs --start`

Skipping steps 1 or 4 will cause data loss or leave the system permanently disabled.

Shared environment:

- `services/systemd/anqr-ops.env`
- `~/.config/systemd/user/anqr-ops.env` after bootstrap install

## Local bootstrap expectations

Required local locations:

- project `.env`
- `~/.config/symphony/anqr.env`
- `~/.config/systemd/user/anqr-ops.env`
- `~/.ssh/*` keys and config when repository access requires them

Optional local support:

- mail configs in the user home directory
- mobile signing material

## Port expectations

- product runtime ports belong to `apps/web`, Netlify, and mobile if later claimed
- harness runtime ports are operator-only and may be absent on reduced developer machines

Documented harness ports:

- `4319` — Symphony agent router (control-plane entrypoint)
- `4320` — Context7 MCP documentation service (POST /v1/resolve-docs, GET /health)
- `4321`-`4328` — Worktree-local Symphony execution bridges (wt1-wt8)
- `18789` — OpenClaw gateway (local AI agent, /v1/chat/completions)
- `18790` — Discord router (load-balances Discord requests to worktree bridges)

Additional port truth must be documented in follow-up runbooks instead of inferred.

## Current runtime notes

- Queue maintenance is split deliberately:
  - runner instances self-feed after issue completion
  - `anqr-queue-feeder.timer` remains a 15-minute safety-net for drain/enforce/backup feed
- Queue feed and drain decisions use `readyDepth` (Todo-only depth), not aggregate queue depth including `In Progress`
- The orchestration runner now requires worktree context; the main repository is control-plane and service-host territory, not the canonical execution working tree

# Workspace Governance

This document defines the fresh Linear workspace model for ANQR 1.0 foundation work.

## Project model

Use a hybrid model:

- projects by stream or package family
- concrete packages tracked by labels/components

Required projects:

- Foundation & Governance
- Documentation & Doctrine
- Harness & Automation
- Web Experience
- API & MCP Delivery
- QR Engine & Core Packages
- Mobile Convergence
- Observability & Reliability
- Release Readiness
- Growth / SEO / Discoverability
- Compliance / Privacy
- Incidents / Ops

## Required labels

- `pkg:contracts`

## Service management protocol

**CRITICAL: Before making ANY changes to bridge services (symphony-bridge, worktree bridges):**

1. **STOP task execution FIRST:**

   ```bash
   node harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-control.mjs --stop
   ```

   - This prevents new tasks from starting while you make changes
   - Without this step, new tasks may start during service restart causing data loss

2. **Wait for zero concurrency:**

   ```bash
   node harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-runner.mjs --status
   ```

   - All worktree runners must be idle (no active leases)
   - Check Discord for "(0 concurrent)" confirmation
   - Typical wait: 5-20 minutes

3. **Make your changes** (restart service, update config, etc.)

4. **RESTART task execution:**

   ```bash
   node harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-control.mjs --start
   ```

   - **CRITICAL:** Without this step, the system remains permanently stopped
   - No work will be processed until timers are re-enabled

**This protocol applies to:**

- Router restart (`systemctl --user restart anqr-symphony-router`)
- Executor restarts (`systemctl --user restart 'anqr-symphony-executor@*.service'`)
- Bridge configuration changes
- Any changes to `harness/ops/integrations/model/*` bridge files
- Provider configuration updates
- Any change that requires service restart

**Why this matters:**

- Restarting bridges during active requests drops streaming connections
- Partial file writes corrupt issue state
- Lost validation results require re-execution
- Wasted provider credits from duplicate API calls

- root `harness/ops/*` entrypoints remain the stable operator contract
- structured subdirectories are the preferred implementation ownership locations
- duplicate or legacy helper locations must not be removed until their replacement path is recorded and accepted

# Provider Routing

This document defines the current provider posture for harness and AI-assisted workflows.

## Principle

Use the cheapest truthful route that satisfies the task while preserving evidence quality.

## Provider Health States

The harness tracks explicit health states for each provider:

- **healthy**: Provider is functioning normally
- **degraded**: Provider is experiencing issues but still usable (1+ consecutive failures)
- **cooling-down**: Provider recently failed, in cooldown period (3+ consecutive failures)
- **disabled**: Provider manually disabled
- **blocked**: Provider blocked from use (e.g., routing loop prevention)
- **unknown**: Provider state not yet determined

Health state transitions are automatic based on consecutive failures/successes:

- 1 failure → degraded
- 3 failures → cooling-down
- 2 successes → healthy

## Timeout Configuration

Provider timeouts are differentiated based on infrastructure type:

- **Local models** (Ollama): 60 seconds
  - Longer timeout accounts for local GPU inference
  - Patterns: `ollama*`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `local-*`
- **Hosted models** (cloud APIs): 30 seconds
  - Faster timeout for cloud API responsiveness
  - All other providers

## Return to Preferred Provider

The system automatically returns to preferred providers (e.g., `codex`) when they become healthy again:

1. Preferred providers are checked first in selection
2. Cooling-down providers are re-probed after cooldown expires
3. Health state is reset to `unknown` after cooldown to allow re-discovery
4. Successful responses transition provider back to `healthy`

Cooldown periods:

- Paid providers (codex, codebuff): 2 minutes
- Free cloud providers: 6 minutes
- Local providers: 2 minutes

## Operating Model

The harness uses a **layered failover model** where each layer handles its own internal fallback:

### Layer 1: OpenClaw (user-facing gateway)

OpenClaw is configured with the following failover chain:

| Priority | Model                                     | Fallback behavior                                         |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary  | `symphony-bridge/symphony/main`           | Symphony autoselects the best healthy provider            |
| 2        | `symphony-bridge/symphony/codex`          | Direct pinned Codex route                                 |
| 3        | `symphony-bridge/symphony/codebuff`       | Direct pinned Codebuff route (SDK inside worktree bridge) |
| 4+       | Other `symphony-bridge/symphony/*` routes | Direct pinned routes matching Symphony inventory          |
| Final    | `ollama/qwen2.5-coder:0.5b`               | Local Ollama fallback                                     |

**Key insight**: OpenClaw should prefer Symphony first, and its fallback inventory mirrors Symphony's provider surface so interactive work keeps going even if the Symphony agent router itself is unavailable.

### Layer 2: Symphony Bridge (credit-gate)

Symphony Bridge uses the credit-gate provider cascade with **tier-based dynamic scoring** based on actual performance metrics and **explicit health state tracking**:

| Tier               | Provider set                                                                                   | Selection method                                                 |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `paid`             | `codex`, `codebuff`                                                                            | Probed first; uses paid API credits; health-aware                |
| `free-cloud`       | `groq`, `mistral`, `gemini*`, OpenRouter (27 models), `sambanova`, `cerebras`, `github-models` | Dynamic scoring with cooldown and re-entry (default tier)        |
| `local-proxy`      | `openclaw`                                                                                     | Local HTTP gateways to other services                            |
| `local-safety-net` | `ollama-local`, `ollama-qwen2.5-coder-3b`, `ollama-qwen2.5-coder-0.5b`                         | Score-capped at 0.25; always rank last in `getRankedProviders()` |

The credit-gate selects providers based on dynamic scoring and health state, with `codex` always retried first when healthy. Provider rotation on failure uses health state tracking to skip cooling-down providers. The exploration mechanism clears old failures every 2-6 minutes (depending on tier) to re-discover providers whose rate-limit windows may have reset.

## Constraint semantics

`allowedNames` and `excludeNames` are authoritative by default.

- Explicit or pinned routes must respect the requested provider set.
- If the requested provider set is exhausted, `selectProvider()` returns `null` by default.
- The local safety-net may bypass those constraints only when the caller explicitly opts in with `allowSafetyNetOverride: true`.

Use `allowSafetyNetOverride: true` only for autonomous production-style execution paths where liveness is more important than strict route pinning.

### Codebuff SDK execution (inside worktree bridges)

When Codebuff is selected by the credit-gate, it runs directly inside the worktree-local Symphony bridge via `codebuff-direct.mjs`:

1. **Paid mode** is always tried first when available.
2. **Free mode** is used if paid mode is unavailable or rate-limited.
3. There is no standalone Codebuff bridge service — the SDK is integrated into each worktree bridge (ADR-0003).

## Current provider cascade

The credit-gate (`symphony-credit-gate.mjs`) owns the shared provider inventory. The harness reaches it only through the Symphony agent router (port 4319), which proxies to worktree-local bridges (ports 4321-4328). OpenClaw uses the same inventory as pinned `symphony/*` routes.

# Quality Gates

This document is the canonical gate reference for ANQR 1.0 foundation work.

## Blocking vs advisory classification

Every harness check is classified as **blocking** or **advisory**.

- **Blocking** checks must pass before merge or promotion. Failure prevents work from proceeding.
- **Advisory** checks are reported and tracked but do not block merge or promotion.

| Check             | Classification | Reason                                                                |
| ----------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `repo-structure`  | blocking       | Foundational — repo cannot function without required dirs/files       |
| `typecheck`       | blocking       | Code correctness — TypeScript must compile                            |
| `lint`            | blocking       | Code quality — oxlint violations are merge-blocking                   |
| `test-unit`       | blocking       | Correctness — unit tests must pass                                    |
| `depcruise`       | blocking       | Architecture — dependency boundaries must hold                        |
| `ast-density`     | blocking       | Architecture — one top-level declaration per file is enforced         |
| `cspell-coverage` | advisory       | Spelling issues are tracked but do not block product work             |
| `docs-freshness`  | advisory       | Stale docs are flagged for review, not merge-blocking                 |
| `ollama-health`   | advisory       | Environment-dependent — only relevant when local AI routing is active |
| `litellm-routing` | advisory       | Environment-dependent — only relevant when provider routing is active |
| `sonar-audit`     | advisory       | Quality insight — informational, not a merge gate                     |

The guardian (`linear-guardian.mjs`) creates issues for all failing checks regardless of classification.
Blocking failures prevent the runner from picking up new work until resolved.
Advisory failures are tracked as backlog items.

### Symphony Bridge (Port 4319)

**Purpose**: OpenAI-compatible gateway with AI SDK for provider communication and tool execution. The harness runner uses this as its only model surface.

**Endpoints**:

- `GET /v1/models` - List models
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` - Chat completion (streaming & non-streaming)
- `GET /health` - Health check (no auth)
- `GET /v1/metrics` - Bridge + credit-gate metrics
- `GET /v1/stats` - Provider statistics

**Configuration**:

- Port: `SYMPHONY_BRIDGE_PORT` (default: 4319)
- Auth: `SYMPHONY_BRIDGE_API_KEY` (default: local-symphony)
- Model: `SYMPHONY_MODEL_ID` (default: symphony/main)

**AI SDK Providers Supported**:

- codebuff (@codebuff/sdk)
- groq (@ai-sdk/groq)
- openrouter (@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider)
- openclaw (OpenAI-compatible)
- mistral (OpenAI-compatible)
- gemini (@ai-sdk/google)
- codex (OpenAI-compatible)

**Tools Available**:

- `exec` - Execute shell commands
- `read` - Read files from filesystem
- `glob` - Find files matching pattern

Tool execution is handled automatically by AI SDK via `maxSteps` (default: 10 iterations).

**Dynamic Tool-Capability Probing**:

At startup, the bridge probes each available provider with a minimal `generateText` call using `toolChoice: "auto"` and a simple `add(2, 2)` tool to determine whether it supports structured tool calling. Providers in `KNOWN_TOOL_CAPABLE` (`codex`, `codebuff`) skip probing entirely and return `known-capable` immediately. Providers that emit raw JSON tool output instead of structured `toolCalls` are excluded from selection. A delayed retry (60s) re-probes rate-limited or errored providers. OpenRouter models share probe results (one probe covers all 27 models).

The `GET /health` endpoint exposes `toolProbe` with:

| Field          | Type       | Description                                                       |
| -------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `capable`      | `string[]` | Providers confirmed to support structured tool calls              |
| `excluded`     | `string[]` | Providers excluded (raw JSON tool output detected)                |
| `unclassified` | `string[]` | Available but not yet classified (rate-limited, errored, timeout) |
| `blocked`      | `object[]` | Providers blocked from bridge, with `{ name, reason }`            |

**Bridge Provider Blocklist**:

- `openclaw` — Blocked to prevent routing loop (bridge → openclaw → bridge)

### Overview

OpenClaw is an external AI agent framework that provides autonomous code editing capabilities. It should prefer Symphony Bridge as the primary route, while keeping pinned fallbacks that mirror Symphony's provider inventory.

### How OpenClaw Uses Symphony and Codebuff

# Adaptive Context and Rate Management

This document defines the fully dynamic adaptive context system used by the Symphony Bridge to manage per-provider context limits, rate budgets, and error-driven feedback loops at runtime.

## Principle

Static context limits waste capacity and cause repeated failures. The adaptive context system observes real provider responses — errors, rate-limit headers, and successes — and continuously adjusts per-provider context ceilings and throttle timers so the bridge learns the true operational envelope of every provider at runtime.

## Module

**Source**: `harness/ops/integrations/model/symphony-adaptive-context.mjs`

**Tests**: `harness/ops/integrations/model/symphony-adaptive-context.spec.ts` (75 tests)

**Run tests**:

```bash
npx vitest run harness/ops/integrations/model/symphony-adaptive-context.spec.ts
```

## Architecture

The adaptive context module sits between the static truncation layer and the bridge's request/response loop:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Symphony Bridge (invokeWithAI)                │
│                                                                 │
│  1. estimateMessagesTokens(rawMessages)                         │
│  2. getEffectiveMaxTokens(providerName) → dynamic ceiling       │
│  3. shouldReduceContextForTPM() → proactive halving if needed   │
│  4. truncateMessagesForProvider(msgs, provider, {               │
│       useTools, maxTokensOverride: effectiveMax })               │
│  5. Send request to provider                                    │
│                                                                 │
│  On SUCCESS:                                                    │
│    recordContextSuccess(providerName)                           │
│    recordTokenUsage(providerName, { inputTokens, outputTokens })│
│                                                                 │
│  On ERROR:                                                      │
│    classifyError(err) → errorType                               │
│    recordErrorType(providerName, errorType)                     │
│    if CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE → parseContextErrorDetails → recordContextError │
│    if RATE_LIMITED → parseRateLimitInfo → recordRateLimit        │
│                                                                 │
│  Provider selection (buildSelectionOptions):                     │
│    getThrottledProviders() → exclude from candidate set         │
│                                                                 │
│  Observability (/v1/stats):                                     │
│    getAdaptiveStats() → per-provider adaptive state snapshot    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### State lifecycle

All adaptive state is **in-memory only** and resets on bridge restart. The static limits in `PROVIDER_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS` (defined in `symphony-bridge-truncation.mjs`) serve as the initial ceiling. The adaptive module overrides them downward when errors are observed and slowly recovers toward the base value on consecutive successes.

## Per-Provider State

Each provider gets an independent state object created on first access:

| Field                         | Type                                     | Description                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `providerName`                | `string`                                 | Provider identifier                                          |
| `baseMaxTokens`               | `number`                                 | Initial ceiling from `PROVIDER_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS` (immutable) |
| `dynamicMaxTokens`            | `number`                                 | Current effective ceiling (mutates on errors/successes)      |
| `consecutiveContextErrors`    | `number`                                 | Running count of context-too-large errors                    |
| `consecutiveContextSuccesses` | `number`                                 | Running count of successful requests (resets on error)       |
| `lastContextErrorAt`          | `number\|null`                           | Epoch ms of most recent context error                        |
| `lastContextSuccessAt`        | `number\|null`                           | Epoch ms of most recent success                              |
| `tokenEvents`                 | `Array<{ts, inputTokens, outputTokens}>` | Sliding window (60s) of token usage                          |
| `requestEvents`               | `Array<{ts}>`                            | Sliding window (60s) of request timestamps                   |

## Feedback Loops

### 1. Context limit shrink (413 / context_length_exceeded)

When a provider returns a context-too-large error:

1. `classifyError(err)` → `CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`
2. `parseContextErrorDetails(err)` extracts `reportedLimit`, `requestedTokens`, `isTpmRelated`, `tpmLimit`
3. `recordContextError(providerName, details)` shrinks `dynamicMaxTokens`:
   - **With precise numbers** (provider reported limit and requested tokens): `dynamicMaxTokens *= (reportedLimit / requestedTokens) * 0.9` (10% safety buffer)
   - **Without precise numbers**: `dynamicMaxTokens *= 0.75` (flat 25% reduction)
   - **Floor**: Never below `MIN_MESSAGE_BUDGET_TOKENS` (1,024 tokens)
4. Next request to this provider uses the reduced ceiling via `getEffectiveMaxTokens()`

**Example**: Groq reports "Requested 13,279, Limit 12,000" → ratio = 12000/13279 = 0.904 → `dynamicMaxTokens *= 0.904 * 0.9 = 0.813` → shrinks from 6,000 to ~4,880.

### 2. Context limit expand (consecutive successes)

When a provider succeeds:

1. `recordContextSuccess(providerName)` increments `consecutiveContextSuccesses`
2. After **3 consecutive successes** (`CONTEXT_EXPAND_THRESHOLD`), if `dynamicMaxTokens < baseMaxTokens`:
   - `dynamicMaxTokens *= 1.05` (5% expansion)
   - Never exceeds `baseMaxTokens`
   - Counter resets to 0
3. Over many successes, the limit converges back to the original base value

**Example**: After shrinking Groq to 4,880 → 3 successes → 5,124 → 3 more → 5,380 → … → eventually back to 6,000.

### 3. Rate-limit throttle (429 / rate_limit)

When a provider returns a rate-limit error:

1. `classifyError(err)` → `RATE_LIMITED`
2. `parseRateLimitInfo(err)` extracts from response headers and error messages:
   - `Retry-After` header → `retryAfterMs`
   - `X-RateLimit-Limit-Requests` → `rpmLimit`
   - `X-RateLimit-Remaining-Requests` → `rpmRemaining`
   - `X-RateLimit-Limit-Tokens` → `tpmLimit`
   - `X-RateLimit-Remaining-Tokens` → `tpmRemaining`
   - `X-RateLimit-Reset-Requests` / `Reset-Tokens` → reset timestamps
   - Error message fallback: `"tokens per minute.*limit (\d+)"` → `tpmLimit`
3. `recordRateLimit(providerName, info)` sets a throttle timer:
   - Duration: parsed `retryAfterMs` or default 30 seconds
   - Maximum: 5 minutes (`RATE_LIMIT_MAX_BACKOFF_MS`)
   - Provider excluded from selection until throttle expires
4. `buildSelectionOptions()` in the bridge calls `getThrottledProviders()` and adds them to the exclude set

### 4. Proactive TPM reduction

Before sending a request, the bridge checks whether the provider is approaching its TPM limit:

1. `estimateMessagesTokens(rawMessages)` estimates input token count
2. `shouldReduceContextForTPM(providerName, estimatedTokens)` checks:
   - Does this provider have a known `tpmLimit`? (learned from headers or error messages)
   - Would `currentTPM + estimatedTokens > tpmLimit * 0.85`? (85% threshold)
3. If yes: `effectiveMax` is halved (minimum 1,000 tokens)
4. This prevents hitting the TPM wall before it happens

### 5. TPM/RPM sliding-window tracking

Every successful request records token usage:

```js
recordTokenUsage(providerName, { inputTokens, outputTokens });
```

- **Token events** and **request events** are stored in 60-second sliding windows
- Window is pruned on every access (events older than 60s are dropped)
- Maximum 512 events per window to bound memory
- Token counts are **estimated from text length** (roughly chars/4 + per-message overhead), not actual provider-reported usage. Output tokens are estimated similarly from response text length.
- `getTokensPerMinute(providerName)` → current TPM
- `getRequestsPerMinute(providerName)` → current RPM

### 6. Error classification

All errors are classified into one of six types:

| Error Type          | Detection                                                                                                                                                               | Triggers                 |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `context_too_large` | HTTP 413, "request too large", "body too large", "context_length_exceeded", "maximum context length", "too many tokens", "token limit", "max size", "input is too long" | Context shrink loop      |
| `rate_limited`      | HTTP 429, "rate_limit", "too many requests", "quota exceeded", "throttled"                                                                                              | Rate-limit throttle loop |
| `auth_error`        | HTTP 401/403, "unauthorized", "invalid api key", "authentication", "forbidden"                                                                                          | Error count tracking     |
| `timeout`           | HTTP 408, "timeout", "timed out", "etimedout", "econnaborted"                                                                                                           | Error count tracking     |
| `server_error`      | HTTP 5xx, "internal server error", "bad gateway", "service unavailable"                                                                                                 | Error count tracking     |
| `unknown`           | None of the above                                                                                                                                                       | Error count tracking     |

The classifier traverses the AI SDK error cause chain to find nested status codes and messages (e.g., `err.cause.cause.statusCode`).

### 3. Pre-request — dynamic ceiling and proactive TPM (invokeWithAI)


### 4. Success path — record success + token usage (both streaming and non-streaming)

Both `invokeWithFallbackStream` and `invokeWithFallback` record success and token usage:

```js

  inputTokens: estimateMessagesTokens(messages),
  outputTokens: Math.ceil((result.text?.length || 0) / 4),
});
```

### 5. Error path — classify, record, and trigger appropriate feedback (both catch blocks)

Both streaming and non-streaming catch blocks perform identical adaptive context classification:

```js
const errorType = classifyError(err);
recordErrorType(provider.name, errorType);
if (errorType === ERROR_TYPES.CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE) {
  const details = parseContextErrorDetails(err);
  recordContextError(provider.name, details);
} else if (errorType === ERROR_TYPES.RATE_LIMITED) {
  const rlInfo = parseRateLimitInfo(err);
  recordRateLimit(provider.name, rlInfo);
}
```

### 6. Stream error interception — fatalStreamError (invokeWithFallbackStream only)

Stream errors arriving as `part.type === "error"` events are classified in-flight. If the error is `CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE` or `RATE_LIMITED`, it is stored as `fatalStreamError` and thrown **after** the stream loop completes. This routes the error through the existing catch block (point 5) so the adaptive system records it and provider fallback activates:

```js
if (part.type === "error") {
  const errorType = classifyError(part.error);
  if (errorType === ERROR_TYPES.CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE || errorType === ERROR_TYPES.RATE_LIMITED) {
    fatalStreamError = part.error;
  }
}
// ... after stream loop:
if (fatalStreamError) throw fatalStreamError;
```

Without this interception, stream errors would bypass the adaptive system entirely — the stream "completes" with a finishReason, the success path records `recordContextSuccess()`, and the provider never learns its limit was exceeded.

### 7. Sticky session clearing on failure (both catch blocks)

When a provider fails, `clearSessionProvider(sessionId)` is called immediately in the catch block so concurrent requests on the same session don't keep trying the broken provider:

```js
clearSessionProvider(sessionId);
```

Previously the sticky was only cleared on the next `buildSelectionOptions` call when the failed provider appeared in the exclude set.

```js
const adaptiveContext = getAdaptiveStats();
// included in the stats response JSON
```
